newsitem.title: JAPAN: August performance mixed for Japan's carmakers.
newsitem.headline: August performance mixed for Japan's carmakers.

text.p: Toyota and Mitsubishi saw their exports race ahead in August but domestic output puttered lower at Mitsubishi and two of Japan's other big five carmakers.

Toyota Motor Corp, Japan's biggest carmaker, said on Friday its output rose nearly eight percent to 204,000 vehicles in August, helped by higher exports. It was the second straight month of year-on-year gains.

Toyota's exports rose 25 percent to 93,000 vehicles in August because shipments to the United States and the Middle East were low last year due to a strong yen. Its overseas production fell 20 percent to 88,000 vehicles, mainly because its Kentucky plant had lower output due to a switch over to the new Camry model, which went into production this month.
Toyota's domestic vehicle sales were also flat against last year but it said production may continue to gain in September due to further export gains.
Honda Motor Co Ltd said its production in Japan rose eight percent from a year earlier to some 73,300 vehicles in August, a second successive month of year-on-year gains.
"The gain in August output stemmed from strong domestic sales and recovering exports," a Honda spokesman said.
Honda's exports this year have generally stood at around 60 to 70 percent of last year's levels, but August exports rose to 92 percent of the figure for August 1995.
It said this was due to resumed exports of the Civic to the United States, where demand for the model has been strong.
Honda said it expected its domestic output to continue to rise in September.
Domestic production at Nissan Motor Co Ltd, Japan's second-biggest maker, fell 13 percent from a year earlier to some 100,800 vehicles due to poor exports and domestic sales.
Its domestic sales fell three percent to 55,000 vehicles in August due to poor demand for sedans, despite strong demand for its recreational vehicles.
Nissan's exports fell 20 percent to 41,000 in August, mainly due to inventory cuts in the United States and Europe.
But Nissan's overseas production in August rose 12 percent to 84,000, reflecting recovering output in its Mexican unit and production of the new Primera model at its British unit.
The new British-made Primera will debut early next month, but Nissan said its overall output was unlikely to pick up in September given slow exports and lower domestic sales.

Mitsubishi Motors Corp's exports rose 12 percent to 33,000 in August, helped by the weaker yen, but its domestic output fell 10 percent to 85,000 and domestic sales fell 22 percent to nearly 42,000. It hopes its domestic sales will pick up in September helped by its new Galant and Legnum models.

Mazda Motor Corp's vehicle production fell 10 percent to 55,000 in August and its exports fell 37 percent to 24,000 due to inventory reduction in North America and Europe. Its domestic sales fell 20 percent to 18,500, despite the popularity of its new Demio wagon in Japan.
